correctness.rationale: A Haar-measurable set may first be replaced by a Borel representative modulo a null set; every countable family of translates then changes only on a countable union of null sets, leaving all admissible costs unchanged. For every admissible countable mixture \(a\), Haar invariance gives \(\int_G a\,d\mu=\alpha\), and Jensen gives \(\int_G -\log_2 a\,d\mu\ge -\log_2\alpha\). For the reverse inequality, independent Haar translates with weights \(2^{-k}\) give a positive-a.e. baseline \(a_0\) with \(\int_G-\log_2a_0\,d\mu\le1/\alpha\) in expectation, hence for some realization. Finite averages of independent translates have binomial pointwise counts; Hoeffding and Fubini give exceptional sets \(B_N\) with measure tending to zero. Mixing each average with \(\varepsilon a_0\) controls the logarithmic cost on \(B_N\) by the integrable function \(-\log_2a_0\). Taking \(N\to\infty\) and then \(\delta,\varepsilon\downarrow0\) proves the matching upper bound. The boundary \(\alpha=1\) is immediate.

value.rationale: This proves a natural case explicitly highlighted in prior work: the countable-mixture value for translates of a positive-measure set. The distinction matters because the cited source notes that for a positive-measure nowhere-dense Cantor set the finite-mixture entropy is infinite, while the unrestricted-mixture value is finite. The theorem shows that countable mixtures recover the exact finite value \(-\log_2\alpha\) throughout the compact-group translate family.
